newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers with tanks go after Liberian rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers with tanks go after Liberian rebels.

text.p: West African peacekeepers with tanks headed for western Liberia on Wednesday to try and clear out guerrillas blocking highways to international relief workers, witnesses said.
Hundreds of troops of the Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping force in 16 trucks sang war songs and waved their weapons as they crossed the Po River bridge outside Monrovia.

Wednesday was the deadline given by ECOMOG commander General Victor Malu for guerrillas of General Roosevelt Johnson's ULIMO-J militia to dismantle roadblocks in the Grand Cape Mount and Bomi counties.

Fighting between ECOMOG and ULIMO-J in the area last December and January was followed by militia warfare in Monrovia in April and May that derailed a 1995 accord on ending nearly seven years of civil war in Liberia.
"We do not expect resistance, but if that happens it would be unfortunate," ECOMOG spokesman Major Patrick Okoh said.
